name: Filesystem
description: Secure local file operations with configurable allow-listed directories — the reference server every local agent starts with.
notes: Always pass an explicit allow-listed root. Running it on `/` gives an agent write access to your whole machine.

name: Fetch
description: Fetches a URL and converts it to clean markdown for the model, with robots.txt respect and chunked reading.

name: Git
description: Read, search and diff a local git repository — history-aware agents without shelling out to raw git.

name: Memory (Knowledge Graph)
description: Persistent knowledge-graph memory stored as local JSON — gives an agent recall across sessions for free.
notes: Pair with a free vector store (Qdrant or Chroma) when the graph grows past a few thousand entities.

name: Sequential Thinking
description: Structured step-by-step reasoning with revision and branching — measurably improves multi-step agent plans.

name: Time
description: Time and timezone conversion grounded in the host clock — stops agents hallucinating dates.

name: Everything (Test Server)
description: Reference server exercising every MCP primitive — the fastest way to test a new client or transport.

name: GitHub MCP Server
description: Repo automation, PRs, issues, code search and CI workflows — the most-starred MCP server in the ecosystem.
notes: A hosted remote variant is available at https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ if you would rather not run Docker.

name: Playwright MCP
description: Browser automation over accessibility snapshots rather than screenshots — deterministic agent browsing in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
notes: Accessibility-tree snapshots use far fewer tokens than screenshot-based browser agents.

name: Chrome DevTools MCP
description: Drives a real Chrome instance for performance traces, console errors and network inspection.

name: Notion MCP
description: Reads and writes Notion pages and databases — the cleanest way to give an agent a knowledge base you already maintain.
notes: Remember to share the specific pages with the integration — a token alone grants nothing.

name: Sentry MCP
description: Pulls issues, stack traces and traces into the prompt so an agent can triage production errors.

name: Supabase MCP
description: Postgres schema, migrations, edge functions and logs through one authenticated server.
notes: Start with --read-only; agents granted DDL rights will eventually drop something you wanted.

name: MongoDB MCP
description: Query, aggregate and inspect collections, including Atlas administration.

name: Redis MCP
description: Key-value access, data structure operations and vector set queries against Redis or Upstash.

name: Cloudflare MCP Servers
description: Fifteen-plus specialised servers for Workers, R2, D1, DNS, logs and Workers AI.
notes: Each Cloudflare product ships its own server; pick the observability or bindings one rather than enabling all of them.

name: Vercel MCP
description: Deployments, build logs, environment variables and project configuration.

name: AWS MCP Servers
description: Official suite covering S3, Lambda, DynamoDB, CloudWatch and 20+ other services.
notes: Scope IAM to a read-only role before letting an agent near your account.

name: Azure MCP Server
description: Natural-language management of Azure resources with Entra ID authentication.

name: Google Cloud MCP Servers
description: Managed MCP endpoints for Cloud Run, BigQuery, Spanner and gcloud workflows.
notes: Google has renamed and reorganised these packages several times in 2026 — confirm the current package name on the docs page before copying the install line.

name: Docker MCP Gateway
description: Container management plus a gateway that catalogs and proxies hundreds of other MCP servers.

name: Kubernetes MCP
description: kubectl-style cluster operations — inspect pods, apply manifests and read logs.
notes: Point it at a non-production context. An agent with cluster-admin is a very efficient way to delete a namespace.

name: Terraform MCP
description: Provider and module registry lookups plus plan/apply assistance for infrastructure as code.

name: Grafana MCP
description: Query dashboards, Loki logs and Prometheus metrics from inside the agent loop.

name: Elasticsearch MCP
description: Search indices and run aggregations; works against Elastic Cloud or self-hosted.

name: Stripe MCP
description: Read customers, invoices and subscriptions, and create payment links from a prompt.
notes: Use a restricted key in test mode. --tools=all grants write access to live objects if the key allows it.

name: Figma MCP
description: Pulls design tokens, layout and component structure out of Figma files into the editor.
notes: Figma also ships a first-party Dev Mode server on localhost:3845 for desktop app users.

name: Linear MCP
description: Create, search and update issues and projects in Linear from the agent loop.

name: Atlassian MCP
description: Jira issues and Confluence pages — the enterprise ticketing counterpart to Linear.

name: Slack MCP
description: Read channels and post messages — the archived reference server's maintained successor.
notes: The original Slack reference server was archived in 2026 and now lives in modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived.

name: Airtable MCP
description: Read and write Airtable bases — a spreadsheet-shaped backend for agent prototypes.

name: Google Workspace MCP
description: Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs and Sheets through a single OAuth'd server.

name: Zapier MCP
description: Bridges an agent to 8,000+ app actions without writing per-service integrations.
notes: Free plan limits how many actions you can expose at once.

name: n8n MCP
description: Gives an agent the full n8n node catalogue so it can build and edit workflows.
auth_type: n8n API key (optional, for live control)

name: Browserbase MCP
description: Cloud browser sessions with stealth mode, proxies and session replay for agents.

name: Apify Actors MCP
description: Runs any of Apify's 5,000+ scrapers as an agent tool, including the free-tier actors.

name: ElevenLabs MCP
description: Text-to-speech generation and voice management inside the agent loop.

name: Hugging Face MCP
description: Searches models, datasets and Spaces, and can call Gradio apps as tools.

name: Qdrant MCP
description: Stores and retrieves memories in a Qdrant collection — vector memory as a tool, in about four lines of config.
notes: Pairs with Qdrant's free 1GB cluster, so long-term agent memory costs nothing to start.

name: Chroma MCP
description: Local or cloud Chroma collections exposed as MCP tools for RAG and memory.

name: Neo4j MCP
description: Cypher queries and graph-schema inspection against AuraDB Free or self-hosted Neo4j.

name: Postgres MCP Pro
description: Read-only-safe Postgres access with index tuning and health checks — the maintained replacement for the archived reference server.
notes: The original @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres reference server was archived in 2025 — many guides still tell you to install it.

name: SQLite MCP
description: Query and inspect a local SQLite file, including business-intelligence style summaries.
notes: Archived but still functional and still the simplest SQLite option. Community forks exist if you need active maintenance.

name: MySQL MCP Server
description: Read-only-by-default MySQL queries and schema inspection.

name: Context7
description: Version-pinned, up-to-date documentation for thousands of libraries — the single highest-value server for coding agents.
notes: Works without a key at low volume; an API key raises the rate limit. The most-installed MCP server on npm.

name: Firecrawl MCP
description: Crawls, scrapes and extracts structured data from sites, returning clean markdown for the model.

name: Exa MCP
description: Semantic web search tuned for agents, with deep-research and company-research modes.

name: Tavily MCP
description: Search, extract and map endpoints purpose-built for LLM grounding, with a genuinely usable free tier.

name: Brave Search MCP
description: Independent web and local search index with a free API tier — no Google/Bing dependency.
notes: Brave's free tier is rate-limited to roughly one query per second and requires a card for verification.

name: DeepWiki MCP
description: Ask questions about any public GitHub repository and get answers grounded in its actual code and wiki.

name: Ref MCP
description: Token-efficient documentation search across technical sites, alternative to Context7.

name: DuckDuckGo MCP
description: Keyless web search and safe text fetching — zero signup, which is rare in search tooling.
notes: Rate-limited by DuckDuckGo itself; fine for occasional lookups, not for bulk crawling.

name: Wikipedia MCP
description: Wikipedia search, article retrieval and section-level summaries.

name: YouTube MCP
description: Fetches video transcripts by URL so agents can reason over talks and tutorials.

name: Obsidian MCP
description: Read and write notes in a local Obsidian vault — a personal knowledge base as agent memory.

name: FastMCP
description: Pythonic framework and CLI for building MCP servers in about ten lines, with a built-in dev inspector.
notes: If you are writing your own server, start here. It also has `fastmcp dev` for interactive testing.

name: OpenAPI MCP Server
description: Turns any OpenAPI/Swagger spec into MCP tools — the fastest path to exposing an existing REST API.

name: AntV Chart MCP
description: Generates charts and dashboards (25+ chart types) as images from natural language data.

name: Puppeteer (Archived)
description: The original browser-automation reference server. Superseded by Playwright MCP.
notes: Still installs and works, but receives no fixes. Use @playwright/mcp for anything new.

name: Google Drive (Archived)
description: Searches and reads Google Drive files. Superseded by community Workspace servers.
notes: Archived in 2025. The community google_workspace_mcp server covers this and more.

name: Slack (Archived Reference)
description: The original Slack channel-management reference server, now unmaintained.
notes: Listed so you can recognise it when a tutorial tells you to install it. Use the Zencoder fork instead.

name: Brave Search (Archived Reference)
description: Archived reference search server, replaced by Brave's own first-party server.
notes: Install @brave/brave-search-mcp-server instead.
